vectors.description: Celik et al. 2008 Table 1 GCI procedure, case 1 (monotonic).

inputs.procedure: p = (1/ln r21) |ln|eps32/eps21| + q(p)|, q(p) = ln[(r21^p - s)/(r32^p - s)], s = sign(eps32/eps21); phi_ext = (r21^p phi1 - phi2)/(r21^p - 1); e_a = |(phi1 - phi2)/phi1|; e_ext = |(phi_ext - phi1)/phi_ext|; GCI_fine = 1.25 e_a/(r21^p - 1)

our_recomputation.foundation_note: foundation recomputation (Python float64, numpy, 2026-11-14, R = N_A k_B = 8.31446261815324 J/(mol K)), not a published value; fixed-point iteration on p

tolerance.unit: p dimensionless, phi_ext in phi units, the three error measures in percent points
tolerance.basis: published values are rounded (p to 2 decimals, percentages to 1 decimal); the note's recomputation agrees with every published key within 0.05 (largest gaps: case 1 p 0.007 and GCI 0.03 points, case 2 e_ext 0.05 points). Assert against our_recomputation within half a unit of its last digit and against the published values within 0.06

vectors.note: Safety factor 1.25 for three grids (MDS50). Used to verify the GCI helper in tests/oracle before it judges the engine integrator.

vectors.description: Number of simulations for a coverage estimate with a target Monte Carlo standard error.
vectors.published_expected_text: 1,900 simulations give Monte Carlo SE 0.5% on a 95% coverage estimate

vectors.description: JCGM 101 minimum number of trials and adaptive batch size for p = 0.95.
vectors.published_expected_text: M "at least 10^4 times greater than 1/(1-p)"; adaptive batches of M = max(J, 10^4), J the smallest integer at least 100/(1-p)
vectors.note: Compute J with exact rational arithmetic: in float64, 100/(1-0.95) = 1999.9999999999995 and 1/(1-0.95) * 1e4 = 199999.99999999997, so a naive ceil or floor can be off by one. Use fractions.Fraction or round to the nearest integer when 1/(1-p) is integral within 1e-9.
